stories.title: Families of 13 children sue hospitals, Michigan doctor over alleged misuse of pediatric medical images
stories.summary: Families of 13 children are suing a Michigan pediatric urologist and two hospitals, alleging the doctor improperly photographed and recorded children's genitals, transferring images to personal accounts. The lawsuit claims hospitals failed to protect patients, with some alleged victims being infants and toddlers. An FBI affidavit cited thousands of files, including child pornography, in the doctor's cloud account.
entities: Mercy Health – St. Vincent Medical Center

stories.title: Controversial Scarecrow Goes Missing
stories.summary: A controversial "Rocky Horror Picture Show" themed scarecrow, sponsored by LGBTQ+ advocacy group PFLAG, was stolen from Plymouth's Kellogg Park around October 16. The scarecrow, which depicted Tim Curry's Dr. Frank-N-Furter, had drawn complaints for its costume and accompanying sign, but also significant community support.

stories.title: 1st Friday Focus on the Environment: Dingell talks environmental policy in a Democrat-controlled Congress
stories.summary: Congresswoman Debbie Dingell announced plans to introduce a 'Data Center Bill of Rights' to address environmental and infrastructure concerns surrounding large-scale data centers in her district. The proposed legislation aims to mandate transparency, independent monitoring, and community benefit agreements.

stories.title: Ann Arbor's iconic Blimpy Burger reopens under new ownership
stories.summary: Ann Arbor's Krazy Jim's Blimpy Burger has reopened following a seven-month closure under new local ownership. The establishment has introduced menu additions, including alcoholic beverages and soft-serve ice cream, while navigating community adjustments to operational changes ahead of a planned mid-November ribbon-cutting.

stories.title: El-Sayed claims victory, wins historic U.S. Senate race
stories.summary: Abdul El-Sayed, former Wayne County and Detroit health director, won Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat, becoming the nation's first Muslim U.S. senator. He defeated Republican Mike Rogers in a hard-fought race, campaigning on a progressive platform focused on healthcare, the environment, and economic issues.

inputFacts.summary: A $250,000 investment from the KeyBank Foundation is expanding shelter and support services for homeless adults in Ypsilanti and eastern Washtenaw County. inputFacts.title: Development Plans Along Five Mile Road
inputFacts.summary: Development along the Five Mile Road corridor in Plymouth and Northville Townships is shifting toward warehouses, condominiums, and offices rather than the high-tech industrial jobs originally envisioned for the Michigan International Technology Center. While infrastructure improvements like water lines and power substations are underway, officials face ongoing challenges regarding road conditions and the types of commercial projects being proposed.

inputFacts.title: The Henry Ford Museum evacuated after reported bomb threat
inputFacts.summary: The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn was evacuated Saturday evening following a reported bomb threat. Police and security personnel searched the facility, and officials have urged the public to avoid the area as the investigation continues.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor uses $180,000 budget to repair city’s aging emergency sirens
inputFacts.summary: The City of Ann Arbor is allocating $180,000 to repair and maintain its emergency siren system. This move reverses a previous decision by the City Council to decommission the sirens earlier this year.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor City Council approves crypto regulations, religious worship protections, $10M park funding
inputFacts.summary: The Ann Arbor City Council passed new regulations for cryptocurrency kiosks, enhanced safety measures for religious institutions, and approved $10 million in funding for park improvements. The new crypto rules include transaction limits and mandatory licensing, while the ordinance for places of worship prohibits obstructive behavior within 50 feet of the premises.

inputFacts.title: Dearborn Mayor says Senate election drives record voter turnout
inputFacts.summary: Dearborn Mayor Abdullah Hammoud reported record-breaking voter turnout in the city during the recent midterm elections. He attributed the surge to the successful campaign of Abdul El-Sayed, who became the first Muslim U.S. Senator, noting that voters were motivated by his focus on working-class issues despite facing significant anti-Arab and anti-Muslim rhetoric.

inputFacts.title: Detroit families affected by fentanyl gather at DEA summit for prevention
inputFacts.summary: Families in Detroit who have lost loved ones to fentanyl gathered at a DEA summit to share their experiences and promote prevention. Attendees emphasized the importance of talking about their loss as part of the healing process.

inputFacts.title: Michigan Attorney General says no charges for deputies who shot Navy veteran
inputFacts.summary: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel announced that no criminal charges will be filed against Washtenaw County deputies involved in the fatal January 2026 shooting of Navy veteran John Jenuwine. While the Attorney General concluded the officers faced a legitimate threat, the family's legal counsel plans to continue with a pending civil lawsuit.

inputFacts.title: $70 million gift excites Michigan tribal college, but funding gaps remain
inputFacts.summary: A $70 million donation from philanthropist MacKenzie Scott to the American Indian College Fund aims to support a seven-year plan for Native American higher education. Despite the gift, leaders at institutions like Saginaw Chippewa Tribal College note that persistent funding gaps and reliance on temporary grants continue to challenge program sustainability.

inputFacts.title: AADL celebrates books and authors with annual Printmaking Festival and A2 Community Bookfest
inputFacts.summary: The Ann Arbor District Library is hosting its annual Printmaking Festival and A2 Community Bookfest. These free events will include author talks, hands-on activities, and a variety of vendors on November 14 and 15, 2026.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor Police Chief Anderson to retire
inputFacts.summary: Ann Arbor Police Chief Andre Anderson is set to retire. He recently addressed the City Council regarding a pilot program for an unarmed crisis response team.
